target_customer: Retail crypto holders who find DeFi investing too complex
problem: Holding tokens is common but using DeFi is hard because of wallet setup, on ramps and risk. Rainmaker offered an account abstraction wallet with email login, bank deposits and gas free one click DeFi strategies.
business_model: Consumer crypto wallet with fees on DeFi strategy usage (not stated by a source)

founders.name: Carlos Reyes Stoneham
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says he led Consumer Growth at LinkedIn Learning and added over 14M in revenue (self reported).

founders.name: Brent Traut
founders.background_notes: VP of Engineering at Hashflow per YC launch post and YC page.

exit.reason: Company site says Rainmaker is officially shut down and users were asked to migrate funds over the past year; no cause given

technical_complexity.rationale: MPC key management, smart contract wallets, gas sponsorship and protocol integrations for a security critical consumer product built by two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Wallet front ends are easy to replicate and users can move funds; the account abstraction standard was not finalized until March 2023 per a secondary source.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source records incumbents copying Rainmaker.

market_need_then: The YC launch post argues most token holders find DeFi too hard to use, pointing to setup, on ramp and investing friction. No dated demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used rainmaker.nyc rather than a plain .com

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain language DeFi for everyone positioning; shutdown page calls it The Airdrop Wallet

branding.community_and_virality: Featured in a Quicknode Feature Fridays post and a Blocmates article; several unrelated products share the name Rainmaker

brand_strength.rationale: Some crypto media coverage but a generic word shared with unrelated products.

outcome_analysis: Rainmaker launched an account abstraction DeFi wallet in YC W23 and later closed. Its site says it is officially shut down after asking users to migrate funds over the last year. No source states why, and no funding history could be verified, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: Funding search returned an aggregator (sig.ai) listing a 2024 seed and a 25M round in 2025 plus 31.3M cumulative, and a Decrypt article on Stackup 4.2M; these appear to mix up other companies named Rainmaker or Stackup and are not recorded as rounds. Shutdown date unknown. Competitor list empty because no dated sources naming rivals were found; the launch post names no competitors. Education not found.
